title: Observation of multipartite spin entanglement in a cuprate chain
authors: S. F. R. TenHuisen, Z. Shen, V. Bhartiya, V. Menon, P. Sharma, H. Padma, Z. Guan, W. He, M. K. Lajer, J. Li, D. Banerjee, J. Pelliciari, I. A. Zaliznyak, G. D. Gu, M. D. Lukin, S. Johnston, M. P. M. Dean, V. Bisogni, Y. Wang, M. Mitrano
abstract: Quantum materials are believed to host highly entangled states of matter, but probing and quantifying such entanglement has long remained experimentally elusive. Here, we use resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) as a probe of multipartite spin entanglement. By projecting the RIXS cross section onto the appropriate spin excitation channel, we show that the Quantum Fisher Information can be extracted directly from the measured spin fluctuation spectrum. We detect at least 7-partite spin entanglement in the model one-dimensional cuprate Sr$_2$CuO$_3$, revealing one of the largest entanglement depths yet reported in a solid. The observed entanglement depth agrees with Hubbard-model expectations and persists to elevated temperatures. Our results establish RIXS as an experimental probe of many-body spin entanglement and provide a platform for extensions to charge and orbital sectors and nonequilibrium settings.
summary: This paper pioneers the use of Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS) to experimentally probe multipartite spin entanglement in cuprate superconductors. By calculating the Quantum Fisher Information from measured spin fluctuations, the authors report detecting at least 7-partite entanglement in the 1D $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{CuO}_3$ model. This establishes RIXS as a powerful, non-invasive spectroscopic tool for characterizing complex quantum states in correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is experimentally probing and quantifying multipartite spin entanglement within quantum materials, which has historically been very difficult.
main_result: The authors report the detection of at least 7-partite spin entanglement in the model 1D cuprate $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{CuO}_3$, establishing RIXS as a viable spectroscopic tool for measuring many-body entanglement.
method: The study uses Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS) to measure spin fluctuation spectra, from which the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) is extracted as a witness for entanglement.
model_or_system: The system studied is the prototypical one-dimensional (1D) cuprate $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{CuO}_3$, modeled by the extended Hubbard model, which reduces to a Heisenberg model in the large-$U$ limit.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) density, entanglement depth, and the spin dynamical structure factor $S(q, \hbar\omega)$.
important_parameters: The entanglement depth is shown to agree with Hubbard-model expectations and persists to elevated temperatures. Key parameters include $t_h \simeq 560 	ext{ meV}$ and $U = 8t_h$.
main_assumptions: The QFI extraction relies on projecting the measured RIXS cross section onto the appropriate spin excitation channel, and the analysis assumes certain sum rules hold for normalization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the RIXS setup and the theoretical description of $	ext{Sr}_2	ext{CuO}_3$ as a 1D Hubbard model. Other figures detail two-spinon excitations, calculated RIXS intensities, and momentum-dependent QFI.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical link between entanglement depth and QFI, details the methodology for extracting QFI from RIXS measurements by projecting the signal onto the spin structure factor, and finally presents the quantitative results showing high-order entanglement in the cuprate model.
why_interesting: This work bridges the gap between abstract quantum information theory (entanglement measures) and tangible solid-state spectroscopy (RIXS), providing a concrete experimental pathway to study quantum correlations in strongly correlated materials.
